screening_decisions.reason: Basic science study examining drug effects on Na+ channels in mammalian cell lines, not a randomised controlled trial in patients with epilepsy.
Prospective observational cohort study identifying factors associated with poor seizure control, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy.

Double-blind randomised trial comparing multiple anticonvulsants including phenobarbital and diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) in patients with focal brain damage and epilepsy. While it compares multiple drugs, it includes the drugs of interest in a randomised design.
Cochrane review about teratogenic effects of AEDs in pregnancy, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for seizure control.
Review article discussing principles of AED therapy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Epidemiological survey estimating prevalence of neurologic disorders, not an RCT comparing treatments.
Randomised controlled trial directly comparing phenobarbital vs phenytoin monotherapy in children aged 2-18 years with partial and generalised tonic-clonic epilepsy. Meets all selection criteria.
Methodology paper describing techniques for extracting statistics for meta-analyses, not a clinical trial.
Meta-analysis estimating global burden of epilepsy, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin.
Randomised controlled trial but compares phenobarbital vs carbamazepine, not phenobarbitone vs phenytoin as required by selection criteria.
Observational study about congenital malformations in children exposed to AEDs in utero, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for seizure control.
Observational registry study describing natural history and prevalence of epilepsy, not an RCT comparing treatments.
Epidemiological study estimating incidence of epilepsy in HMO populations, not an RCT comparing treatments.
Review article summarizing literature on behavioral and cognitive effects of AEDs, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin.
Methodology chapter from Cochrane handbook about assessing risk of bias, not a clinical trial.
Observational registry study about congenital malformations from AED exposure in pregnancy, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for seizure control.
Review article discussing diagnostic accuracy and case ascertainment in epilepsy epidemiology, not an RCT.
Review article about dermatological applications of phenytoin, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for epilepsy.
Basic science study examining GABA receptor modulation in cell cultures, not a randomised controlled trial in patients.
Animal study examining folate metabolism with phenytoin in rats, not an RCT in human patients with epilepsy.

This is a prospective community-based cohort study, not a randomised controlled trial. It examines prognostic factors for remission of epilepsy rather than comparing phenobarbitone versus phenytoin monotherapy.

This is a randomised study where patients were randomly assigned to monotherapy with carbamazepine, phenytoin, or phenobarbitone. It includes direct comparison of phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy in patients with epilepsy. Although the primary outcomes are cognitive effects rather than seizure control, it provides relevant IPD for the comparison of interest.
This study evaluates combination therapy (carbamazepine combined with phenytoin and/or phenobarbital), not monotherapy. The selection criteria specifically require monotherapy comparisons.

This is a 10-center, double-blind randomised controlled trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs as monotherapy in 622 adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. It includes phenobarbital and phenytoin monotherapy arms, matching the selection criteria perfectly.
This is a methodological paper describing statistical methods for meta-analysis. It uses epilepsy trials as illustrations but is not itself a randomised controlled trial.

This is a randomised, double-blind clinical trial comparing phenobarbitone, phenytoin, and sodium valproate as monotherapy in 151 children with generalized tonic-clonic seizures aged 4-12 years. It directly compares phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy in the target population.
This is a methodological paper examining outcome reporting bias in Cochrane reviews. It is not a randomised controlled trial of antiepileptic drugs.
This is a methodological paper discussing principles of equivalence trial design. It is not a clinical trial of antiepileptic drugs.
This is a population-based incidence study, not a randomised controlled trial. It examines epidemiology and syndrome classification rather than comparing antiepileptic drug treatments.
This is a methodological paper about measuring heterogeneity/inconsistency in meta-analyses. It is not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a guideline paper introducing the PRISMA statement for reporting systematic reviews. It is not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a review article describing the pharmacological mechanisms of various antiepileptic drugs. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This is a prospective randomised pragmatic trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs as monotherapy in 243 adult patients (aged 16+) with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial with or without secondary generalised seizures. It includes phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy arms, matching the selection criteria perfectly.

This is a randomised double-blind, triple crossover study comparing carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and phenytoin in 15 patients with partial complex epilepsy. Each patient received each drug as monotherapy for 3 months. It provides direct comparison of phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy in patients with focal onset seizures.

This is a controlled trial evaluating carbamazepine. While it mentions comparison with phenobarbital or diphenylhydantoin, the abstract indicates patients were already on combination therapy. It does not appear to be a monotherapy comparison of phenobarbitone versus phenytoin.
This is a position paper updating the ILAE classification system for epilepsies. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This is a network meta-analysis (systematic review) synthesizing data from multiple trials. While it includes phenobarbitone and phenytoin comparisons, it is a secondary analysis, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
This is a network meta-analysis synthesizing individual patient data from 20 randomised trials. It is a secondary analysis/meta-analysis, not a primary randomised controlled trial.

This is a controlled study evaluating carbamazepine in patients whose seizures were not controlled by existing combination therapy. It is not a monotherapy comparison of phenobarbitone versus phenytoin.
This is a Cochrane systematic review examining neurodevelopmental outcomes in children exposed to AEDs in utero. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Basic science mechanistic study using mouse neuroblastoma cells, not an RCT in human patients.
Epidemiological incidence study, not an RCT with drug treatment comparison.
Methodological paper, not a primary RCT comparing phenobarbitone versus phenytoin.
Preclinical basic science study in rat neurons, not an RCT in human patients.
RCT comparing phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy in children with newly diagnosed epilepsy matching inclusion criteria.
